subject: Lexical elements
notes: Rule: 'The separator space may optionally immediately follow any separator except the opening delimiter of a literal. A space following the opening delimiter of a literal is part of the literal and not a separator.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 9)). STR_BODY takes every character after the opening quote into the literal. Probes: litspaces.cob `MOVE " B" TO A` then `DISPLAY "[" A "]"` prints '[ B   ]' (leading space kept); `A( 3 :)` / `E( 3 )` / `LOWER-CASE( "CD" )` (spaces after '(' ) accepted; replsp.cob `REPLACE == XX == BY == DISPLAY ==.` (space after opening pseudo-text delimiter) prints OK. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs#ReadReplaceOperand (the symbol was removed by kb/Work PB1350/PB1354; the successor that now implements the same step is named in its place (verdict untouched — the row is another note's)) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4#SUB_WS (kb/Work PB2113 deleted the SUBSCRIPT lexer mode; inside a list region the separator and its following spaces are one FNARG_SEPARATOR token)
